newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end mixed, erasing early gains.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end mixed, erasing early gains.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures closed mixed on Wednesday, as some contracts erased earlier gains on technically driven selling from local investors, traders said.
Prices ranged from 50 yen lower to 90 yen higher, with the benchmark March 1998 contract down 50 yen at 16,320 yen per tonne. The day's volume was 34,542 lots.
All contracts rose early, reflecting the dollar's gains, traders said. The dollar rose to about 126.70 yen in afternoon Tokyo trade, up from 125.90 yen late on Monday afternoon.
Bullish sentiment in the corn market dissipated, however, and some contracts fell back by the close, traders said.

On CBOT Project A, the spot May corn contract was trading at $2.99 per bushel at 0810 GMT, off marginally from $2.99-1/2 at Tuesday's close. Spot May CBOT soybean futures were at $8.47-3/4 per bushel on the overnight trading system, down from $8.49-1/4 at Tuesday's close.
